provenance: Topic introductions and formula explanations identify existing project calculator conventions. Only result text verified against completed PDFs is published as a reading. Pending result profiles remain placeholders.

topics.name: Personality
topics.overview: The Personality number is read as your outward presentation: the qualities people may notice first and the impression you make. It focuses on the way you meet others, rather than every part of your character.
steps: Use your full name at birth, including all middle names.
Take the consonants in each name word and add their Pythagorean values.
Reduce each word’s consonant total, keeping 11, 22, or 33 when reached. Add those reduced totals, then reduce again by the same rule.
topics.convention_note: Use repeating Pythagorean letter values (A=1 through I=9, then J=1 again). Crystaleye counts A, E, I, O, U as vowels and Y as a consonant. Accented Latin letters are normalized; spaces separate name words, while apostrophes and hyphens within a word are ignored. Other traditions can classify letters or reduce totals differently.

topics.name: Minor Personality
topics.overview: Minor Personality applies an outward-impression reading to the name you currently use. It offers an everyday-name perspective alongside, rather than a replacement for, your birth-name Personality.
steps: Use the current first, middle, and last names you actually supply to the full calculator. If you do not supply a different name, it uses your birth name.
Select consonants, total each name word, and reduce each word while keeping 11, 22, and 33.
Add the reduced word totals and reduce the result with the same master-number rule.
topics.convention_note: Use repeating Pythagorean letter values (A=1 through I=9, then J=1 again). Crystaleye counts A, E, I, O, U as vowels and Y as a consonant. Accented Latin letters are normalized; spaces separate name words, while apostrophes and hyphens within a word are ignored. Other traditions can classify letters or reduce totals differently.

topics.name: Soul’s Desire
topics.overview: Also called Soul Urge or Heart’s Desire, this number is read as inner motivation: what feels fulfilling, what you value, and the desires behind your choices.
steps: Use the full name at birth.
Add only A, E, I, O, U in each name word; reduce the word totals while keeping 11, 22, and 33.
Add those reduced vowel totals and reduce again, retaining a final 11, 22, or 33.
topics.convention_note: Use repeating Pythagorean letter values (A=1 through I=9, then J=1 again). Crystaleye counts A, E, I, O, U as vowels and Y as a consonant. Accented Latin letters are normalized; spaces separate name words, while apostrophes and hyphens within a word are ignored. Other traditions can classify letters or reduce totals differently. A name with no counted vowels has no interpreted Soul’s Desire result in these guides.

topics.name: Minor Soul’s Desire
topics.overview: Minor Soul’s Desire reads the vowels of your current name as an everyday lens on motivation and fulfillment. It is distinct from how the same name may come across to other people.
steps: Use your supplied current name, or the birth name if no alternative is entered.
Add A, E, I, O, U in each word and reduce the word totals, preserving 11, 22, and 33.
Add the reduced totals and reduce again with the same rule.
topics.convention_note: Use repeating Pythagorean letter values (A=1 through I=9, then J=1 again). Crystaleye counts A, E, I, O, U as vowels and Y as a consonant. Accented Latin letters are normalized; spaces separate name words, while apostrophes and hyphens within a word are ignored. Other traditions can classify letters or reduce totals differently. The guide’s 33 profile is an explicitly labeled current-name adaptation; it is not a second directly sourced Minor 33 series.

topics.name: Life Path
topics.overview: Life Path is interpreted as a broad developmental theme: qualities to cultivate, recurring tensions to consider, and possible directions for growth. It is calculated from your full date of birth.
steps: Reduce the birth month, day, and four-digit year separately, keeping 11, 22, and 33 when reached.
Add those three reduced components.
Reduce the combined total, again preserving a final 11, 22, or 33.
topics.convention_note: Example: October 22, 1980 → month 10→1; day 22 stays 22; year 1980→18→9. Then 1+22+9=32→5. This component method matches the existing calculator; other schools use different procedures.

topics.name: Destiny / Expression
topics.overview: Destiny or Expression is read as the capacities and forms of contribution associated with a birth name. The completed guide uses an all-letter Expression calculation. Crystaleye’s calculator uses its established Personality-plus-Soul’s-Desire variant.
steps: For the completed Expression guide, add all letter values in each full birth-name word.
Reduce each word’s total while preserving 11, 22, and 33.
Combine the reduced word totals and reduce again. The quick and full calculators instead reduce Personality + Soul’s Desire.
topics.convention_note: These procedures can disagree on master totals. For Thomas Ann, the guide’s all-letter method gives 33/6 while the established calculator gives Destiny 6. Result pages below reproduce the Expression guide; the calculator labels its method explicitly.

topics.name: Balance
topics.overview: Balance is interpreted as a constructive response to draw on when difficulty disrupts your usual way of handling things. It is an invitation to choose a response, rather than a fixed personality label.
steps: Take the first letter of each word in the full birth name, including entered middle-name words.
Add the Pythagorean values of those initials.
For the completed guide, reduce fully to 1–9, including 11→2, 22→4, and 33→6.
topics.convention_note: The established full calculator keeps 11, 22, and 33 for Balance. Use guide 2 for app 11, guide 4 for app 22, and guide 6 for app 33. These routes explain the mapping; they do not invent separate master Balance profiles.

topics.name: Karmic Lessons
topics.overview: Karmic Lessons identifies the letter-value categories missing from the full birth name. The tradition treats them as reflection themes; missing values do not establish a deficiency, past-life debt, or deserved hardship.
steps: Convert every birth-name letter to its repeating Pythagorean value, 1–9.
Count which values appear.
The absent values form the lesson set. Several lessons, or no lessons, are possible; do not add or reduce that set.
topics.convention_note: The research draft is not a completed guide. Profiles here remain placeholders until its final guide is approved. None is an empty set, not Lesson 0. Masters 11, 22, and 33 are not lesson members.

topics.name: Hidden Passion
topics.overview: Hidden Passion identifies the most frequently repeated birth-name letter value. It is commonly interpreted as a theme of recurring interest or emphasis. Detailed result interpretations are awaiting their guide.
steps: Convert all letters in the full birth name to values 1–9.
Count every occurrence of each value.
Find the highest count. If values tie for the highest count, keep all of them; do not add them together.
topics.convention_note: This explains the existing calculator’s frequency rule. A set of tied values is not a new combined number. Detailed researched profiles have not been published.

topics.name: Birthday
topics.overview: Birthday focuses on the calendar day on which you were born. In this project it keeps the original day as its own chart value, allowing a Birthday 17 to remain distinct from a reduced 8.
steps: Take the day from the recorded birth date.
Keep it as a whole number from 1 through 31.
Do not reduce it for this chart position. The guide will explain any compound-number reading when that content is ready.
topics.convention_note: The full calculator preserves the birth day. Birthday 11 and 22 are day values here; no separate master-number ranking is implied. Birthday 33 is impossible on the calendar.

topics.name: First Life Cycle
topics.overview: The first Life Cycle is one of three date-derived positions used to reflect on broad phases of development. This position uses the birth month; its researched interpretation and timing guide are still to come.
steps: Take the birth month.
Reduce by adding digits until a single digit or retained master 11, 22, or 33 is reached.
Use that result for this cycle position; do not combine it with the other cycle values.
topics.convention_note: This is the existing calculator’s component rule. The first cycle comes from month, the second from day, and the third from year. Result availability reflects the calculator’s current 1800–2026 birth-year range; no cycle ages are assigned here.

topics.name: First Pinnacle
topics.overview: The first Pinnacle is one of four date-derived positions traditionally used as an experience or development theme. Its own researched result descriptions and timing conventions are pending.
steps: Reduce birth month, day, and year separately, preserving 11, 22, and 33.
Add reduced birth month + reduced birth day.
Reduce that total again, retaining 11, 22, or 33.
topics.convention_note: This page explains the established calculator’s formula. The Third Pinnacle combines the already calculated first and second Pinnacles. Detailed timing and result interpretations will be supplied with the corresponding guide.

topics.name: First Challenge
topics.overview: The first Challenge is a date-derived chart position used as a reflection on a developmental tension. A detailed guide for this particular position has not been completed.
steps: For this app, reduce the month, day, and year with 11, 22, and 33 retained.
Calculate reduced month minus reduced day.
If the difference is negative, use zero. Keep the resulting whole number without further reduction.
topics.convention_note: This is Crystaleye’s custom calculator rule. Other numerology methods often use absolute differences after full single-digit reduction. Retaining masters can make this app’s unreduced differences exceed 9. The 0–9 routes and reserved master routes do not substitute a generic number meaning for an unpublished Challenge interpretation.
